security_audit.summary: Most static external-command hits are Markdown formatting or examples, not hidden shell execution. Several belt CLI examples and outbound HTTP examples are real, and the skill intentionally provides hosted arbitrary Python execution through belt. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: Broad hosted code execution through belt
remediation.suggestion: Document that code and inputs are sent to inference.sh, and require user approval before running network or file-heavy tasks.

remediation.issue: External CLI and related skill installation steps
remediation.suggestion: Pin installation sources or versions where possible, and tell users to verify belt and npx install commands before running them.
Add guidance about permitted targets, rate limits, robots.txt, and avoiding secrets in API or scraping requests.

content.user_title: Run Python Tasks in a Hosted Sandbox
content.value_statement: Many agent workflows need Python for data, media, and automation tasks without local setup. This skill routes Python code to a hosted inference.sh environment with common libraries preinstalled.
actual_capabilities: Runs Python snippets through the belt app run workflow for infsh/python-executor.
Provides common data, scraping, media, document, and 3D Python libraries.
Supports configurable execution timeouts from 1 to 300 seconds.
Returns files saved under the outputs directory.
Offers default and high-memory variants with 8 GB or 16 GB RAM.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and an authenticated account.
Runs CPU-only workloads and does not include GPU or dedicated ML libraries.
Non-interactive scripts must save plots and files instead of opening windows.
Network requests depend on remote service policy and target site availability.

use_cases.title: Analyze Datasets
use_cases.description: Load tabular data, compute summaries, and return charts or files from a hosted Python run.

use_cases.title: Automate Web Data Collection
use_cases.description: Fetch public pages or APIs, parse useful fields, and return structured results for review.

use_cases.title: Generate Media and Documents
use_cases.description: Create images, videos, PDFs, or 3D files with preinstalled Python libraries.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Simple Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to run a short Python calculation and report the printed result.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a CSV
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to inspect my CSV file, summarize columns, and save one chart to outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Scrape a Public Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to fetch a public webpage, extract the title and key links, and explain any request failures.

prompt_templates.title: Create Advanced Artifacts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor high memory when needed to generate image, video, or 3D output files and return the artifacts.

output_examples.input: Analyze a small sales table and create a bar chart.
output: Returns a chart file from outputs.

output_examples.input: Fetch a public API profile and summarize selected fields.

output_examples.output: Returns an image file and a short note describing its size and format.

best_practices: Review Python code before execution, especially network and file operations.
Save generated artifacts under outputs so the service can return them.
Set timeouts that match workload size and use high memory only when needed.
anti_patterns: Sending secrets, tokens, or private data unless the remote environment is approved.
Running broad web scraping against sites without permission or rate limits.
Treating the hosted sandbox as a persistent or interactive desktop session.

faq.question: Does this run Python on my local machine?
faq.answer: No. The skill uses inference.sh hosted execution through the belt CLI.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: You need the belt CLI, an authenticated inference.sh account, and access to the python-executor app.

faq.question: Can it access the internet?
faq.answer: Yes, the examples include HTTP requests and API calls. Review each network request before execution.

faq.question: How are generated files returned?
faq.answer: Files saved under outputs are detected by the service and returned with the run result.

faq.question: Does it support GPU workloads?
faq.answer: No. The documented environment is CPU-only and intended for general Python workloads.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive data?
faq.answer: Use sensitive data only if you are authorized to send it to inference.sh and the executed code is reviewed.
